output.brief: The gap is mostly explained by time in level, not by where people work. Remote hiring only opened widely in July 2024, so 230 of 340 remote staff (68%) lack the 18 months in level the policy requires, versus 200 of 760 office staff (26%). Among eligible people, nomination rates (28.6% vs 28.2%), approval rates (73.8% vs 71.0%) and promotion rates (21.1% vs 20.0%) are nearly the same. Remote attrition is not higher (10.9% vs 11.6%), so leaving isn't the cause. The eligible remote group is small (110), so a modest real bias can't be ruled out. Manager comments hint at unequal access to visible work, but that is unmeasured. I'm fairly confident the COO's proposal would be unjustified and would penalise people hired on home-based contracts. Next steps: hold the three-day rule. Report promotion rates for eligible employees only. Re-check at FY2027 with larger numbers. Meanwhile, collect data on who gets stretch assignments, and tell remote staff the eligibility rules; they report less understanding of promotion criteria.
